scenes.headline: How one agent server keeps accounts apart
scenes.sub: Octop: many users, many agents, one process
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Upma! Tencent's new workspace runs many people's agents in one process. Here is what keeps the accounts apart.

scenes.text: Accounts are separated by an owner check on every route; an agent's own shell is contained only if you pick a jail or a container.
scenes.mark: only if you pick a jail or a container
scenes.say: Accounts are separated by an owner check on every route. An agent's shell is contained only if you choose a jail or a container.

steps.say: Every request carries a login token, and each route checks that you own the agent. An admin skips the check.
One registry, in the same process, runs everyone's agents.
Each agent gets a workspace folder in the server's home directory.
By default, an agent's commands run as the server's own user. To the operating system, every folder has one owner.

left.title: The default backend
items: Its root is the host's root
A pattern guard flags risky commands
left.say: By default, commands run as the server's user, rooted at the host, with only a pattern guard.

right.title: A jail or a container
items: Bubble wrap mounts only your folder
Container network is off by default
right.say: An admin can give a user a bubble wrap jail, or give each agent a container with the network off.

scenes.title: Same page, different scopes
scenes.say: These tools look per agent. Each has its own scope.

items.say: The terminal is a host shell, whatever the backend.
The browser keeps one profile per user.
The desktop is the host's one screen.
Coding agents are spawned by the server, on the host.

scenes.title: The desktop page says so itself

steps.say: The desktop page says it: view and control the host's desktop.
It captures this machine's screen and injects keyboard and mouse.

scenes.label: regex rules screen the agent's shell commands
scenes.say: Twenty regex rules screen shell commands. They decide what to ask you. They are not a wall.

scenes.text: The login keeps accounts apart in the app. On disk, only a jail or a container does.
scenes.mark: only a jail or a container does
scenes.say: The login keeps accounts apart in the app. On disk, only a jail or a container does.

recap: Default commands run as the server
Turn on the jail or container
scenes.say: An owner check separates accounts. By default, commands run as the server. Turn on a jail or a container before you invite anyone.
